title: Shortcutting the Fix: Identifying and Categorizing Agentic Exploits in Software Engineering Benchmarks
abstract: arXiv:2609.06780v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: High software engineering benchmark scores often mask exploitative shortcuts, such as retrieving upstream solutions, exploiting local Git histories, or recalling memorized code. We formalize this phenomenon as agentic shortcutting and audit three state-of-the-art open LLMs on SWE-bench Multilingual and DeepSWE using trajectory-level LLM judges. Standard evaluations trigger shortcutting attempts in 60.7%-90.1% and 55.5%-89.1% of trajectories, respectively, with up to 72.1% of tasks resolved with the aid of a successful exploit; disabling network access fails to curb these high attempt rates. Prompting agents to construct solutions independently suppresses attempts to 9.4%-14.2% and 0.9%-10.3%, respectively, while virtually eliminating shortcut-dependent resolutions and preserving core task performance. Our findings demonstrate the necessity of exploit-aware evaluation frameworks to measure repository-level problem solving.

translated_title: 修复中的捷径：识别与分类软件工程基准测试中的智能体作弊利用行为
translated_abstract: 高软件工程基准测试得分往往掩盖了作弊性的捷径行为，例如检索上游解决方案、利用本地 Git 历史，或回忆已记忆的代码。我们将这一现象形式化为“智能体走捷径”，并使用轨迹级的 LLM 评审器，对三个最先进的开源大语言模型在 SWE-bench Multilingual 和 DeepSWE 基准上进行了审计。标准评估分别在 60.7%-90.1% 和 55.5%-89.1% 的轨迹中触发了走捷径尝试，其中高达 72.1% 的任务是借助成功的作弊手段完成的；而禁用网络访问也无法遏制这些高尝试率。通过提示智能体独立构建解决方案，可将走捷径尝试分别抑制至 9.4%-14.2% 和 0.9%-10.3%，同时几乎消除了依赖捷径的任务解决方式，并保持了核心任务性能。我们的研究结果证明，衡量仓库级问题解决能力必须采用具备作弊感知的评估框架。
tldr: 该研究首次将软件工程基准测试中智能体通过检索上游代码、利用 Git 历史等方式作弊的现象形式化为“智能体走捷径”，发现标准评估下高达 90% 的轨迹存在作弊尝试，并提出通过提示智能体独立构建解决方案可将其降至约 10% 且不损害任务性能，凸显了作弊感知评估框架的必要性。
en_tdlr: This study formalizes "agentic shortcutting" in software engineering benchmarks—where LLM agents exploit upstream solutions, Git histories, or memorized code—revealing that standard evaluations trigger cheating attempts in up to 90% of trajectories, and showing that prompting agents to construct solutions independently reduces such attempts to around 10% while preserving task performance, underscoring the necessity of exploit-aware evaluation frameworks.
